body: use `typing.List` for now in this case.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **main** branch:

**dont assume copy_with() on builtins list, dict, etc.** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/4364

You're welcome, thank you! I will keep `typing.List` for now.
Can we also support `collections.abc.Sequence` and `collection.abc.MutableSequence`?
First would valuable if one wants to prevent appending new items to the field. Could also play nice with `relationship`s with `viewonly=True`.
it's the same issue so this fixes them.  I'll add to the test cases

Yes, at the moment we can't do:
`some_relationship: Mapped[Sequence[SomeModel]] = relationship(...)`
`some_relationship: Mapped[MutableSequence[SomeModel]] = relationship(...)`
Just `list[SomeModel]` works, but this is not related to `from __future__ import annotations`.
Trying to do above things result in:
```
sqlalchemy.exc.InvalidRequestError: One or more mappers failed to initialize - can't proceed with initialization of other mappers
```
`Sequence` would be great for read-only relationships
`MutableSequence` would be great for relationships where we can `append`.
As far as I understand, actual type to what SQLAlchemy maps those relationships is not `list`, but some internal type that supports `Sequence` or `MutableSequence` interfaces. Thanks!

> Yes, at the moment we can't do: `some_relationship: Mapped[Sequence[SomeModel]] = relationship(...)` `some_relationship: Mapped[MutableSequence[SomeModel]] = relationship(...)` Just `list[SomeModel]` works, but this is not related to `from __future__ import annotations`. Trying to do above things result in:

you can do these without issue, you just need to tell it what kind of collection to *instantiate*, since it doesn't know that:

```py
from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Sequence

from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped
from sqlalchemy.orm import mapped_column
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


class A(Base):
    __tablename__ = "a"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    data: Mapped[str]
    bs: Mapped[Sequence[B]] = relationship(collection_class=list)


class B(Base):
    __tablename__ = "b"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    a_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("a.id"))
    data: Mapped[str]


print(select(A).join(A.bs))
```

needs a better error message that's all

Oh, yes, it works, sorry for bringing this up. Yes, better error message would be great.
It would be nicer if we could use `list` by default here, if not, current approach is good as well.

the thing is you know this is a list so you can use list[] directly.   If you're trying to imply non-mutability, then having to express the type and the instantiation seems fairly reasonable.   we'd have to make a type map for relationships to automate this, that can be later on.
Yes, I totally agree. Automation here would be nice, but generally not required. Later on sounds great, thank you!

issue.body:
Verify and test that collections.abc generics and native genericts (`list[str]`, `dict[str,int]` etc) are supported in the orm mapping ### Discussed in https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/discussions/9901
Originally posted by **AlexanderPodorov** June 6, 2023 Consider the following setup: ```python from __future__ import annotations # works # from typing import Sequence # fails from collections.abc import Sequence from sqlalchemy import JSON from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import JSONB from sqlalchemy import create_engine from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped from sqlalchemy.orm import mapped_column from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship from sqlalchemy.orm import Session from sqlalchemy.schema import CreateTable from sqlalchemy.dialects import postgresql class Base(DeclarativeBase): type_annotation_map={ Sequence[str]: JSON().with_variant(JSONB(), 'postgresql'), } class User(Base): __tablename__ = "a" id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True) endpoints: Mapped[Sequence[str]] = mapped_column() print(CreateTable(User.__table__).compile(dialect=postgresql.dialect())) ``` This code throws the following error: ``` sqlalchemy.exc.ArgumentError: Could not locate SQLAlchemy Core type for Python type collections.abc.Sequence['str'] inside the 'endpoints' attribute Mapped annotation ``` When `Sequence[str]` is replaced with `Sequence['str']`, then the code works, however it could be nicer not to use quotes. If `Sequence[str]` is wrapped into `Annotated[Sequence[str], 0]` and replaced in all respective places, it works. P.S. May be related to [this issue](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/9099) Thanks!
